newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB raises pulse pool prices on Indian crop fears.
newsitem.headline: AWB raises pulse pool prices on Indian crop fears.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB), Australia's largest pulse marketer, has increased its estimated prices for 1996/97 pulse pools by up to A$10.00 a tonne because of production concerns emerging on the Indian sub-continent, it said in a statement.
The AWB also said it was urging growers to consider chickpeas this season as international demand was predicted to continue through 1997/98.

AWB senior pulse merchant Peter Wilson said prices for chickpeas and field peas had risen rapidly over recent weeks following reports that India's annual chickpea (gram) crop could be down by as much as 25 percent.
"The shortfall in Indian production has only become evident since harvest was completed late last month," he said.

The AWB chickpea pool has been revised up by A$10.00 a tonne to SA$238.00-A$250.00 a tonne delivered port. The AWB field peas pool estimate has also been increased by A$5.00 a tonne to A$220.00-A$230.00 delivered port.
The AWB faba bean pool has been revised up by A$2.00 a tonne to A$230.00-A$245.00 a tonne delivered port.
AWB had been able to extract reasonable returns for faba beans from the market despite limited activity, Wilson said.

Australian faba beans generally traded into Middle Eastern markets, which recently had been quiet. AWB had recently completed discharge of the MV Korean Pigeon, which carried Victorian faba beans to Egypt, he said.
